title: Request for Prospective Tariff Waiver, et al. of Foundry Works Solar Energy LLC under ER26-3713.

documents.text:
UNITED STATES OF AMERICA
                                      BEFORE THE
                        FEDERAL ENERGY REGULATORY COMMISSION


    Foundry Works Solar Energy LLC                  )                Docket No. ER26-____-000



      REQUEST OF FOUNDRY WORKS SOLAR ENERGY LLC FOR PROSPECTIVE
                  TARIFF WAIVER AND EXPEDITED ACTION

           Pursuant to Rules 212 and 207(a)(5) of the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission’s

(“FERC” or “Commission”) Rules of Practice and Procedure,1 Foundry Works Solar Energy LLC

(“Foundry Works”) respectfully requests that the Commission grant a prospective waiver of

Section 4.4.4 of Attachment X of the Midcontinent Independent System Operator, Inc.’s (“MISO”)

Open Access Transmission, Energy and Operating Reserve Markets Tariff (“Tariff”), and Article

2.3.1 of Foundry Works’ Generator Interconnection Agreement (“GIA”) to permit a commercial

operation date of December 15, 2028.

           Foundry Works has been developing a 200 megawatt (“MW”) solar generation facility in

Lake County, Indiana, a region of the country experiencing heightened resource adequacy

concerns. Foundry Works has been diligently pursuing the Project’s development and submitted a

generator replacement request, which MISO approved, to convert the project to a 200 MW battery

energy storage system (“Project”) to support the needs of Indianapolis Power & Light Company

d/b/a AES Indiana (“AES Indiana”). AES Indiana is a vertically integrated utility operating within

MISO that provides electric service to approximately 534,000 retail customers in the city of

Indianapolis and neighboring cities, towns and communities, and adjacent rural areas all within

the state of Indiana. AES Indiana has executed an agreement to purchase Foundry Works and use



1
    18 C.F.R. §§ 385.207(a)(5), 385.212.

                                                1

DCACTIVE-88090505.7
 the Project to serve its load, including data center load. Given the BESS development and

construction timeline, Foundry Works currently anticipates that the Project will be unable to

achieve commercial operation by the GIA’s December 15, 2027 deadline.

        Foundry Works therefore respectfully requests that the Commission grant waiver of

Section 4.4.4 of Attachment X of the MISO Tariff and Article 2.3.1 of the GIA to extend the

commercial operation date by one year, to December 15, 2028. Under Section 3.3.1 of MISO’s

Generator Interconnection Procedures, when a project completes the generator replacement

process, MISO retains the commercial operation date from the existing GIA into the replacement

GIA.2 As such, granting this waiver will ensure that the Project’s replacement GIA reflects a COD

that accommodates the BESS project’s development and construction timeline.3 Unless the

Commission grants this waiver request, MISO will be obligated to terminate Foundry Works’

interconnection agreement if the Project does not achieve commercial operation by December 15,

2027, which would eliminate the Project’s existing interconnection rights and deprive AES Indiana

of a capacity resource intended to meet its growing capacity requirements. Granting the requested

waiver will provide Foundry Works with sufficient time to complete construction of the Project

without facing GIA termination, enabling the Project to contribute to the resource adequacy needs

of the region and AES Indiana.

        Foundry Works is authorized to represent that MISO supports this waiver request and that

Northern Indiana Public Service Company LLC (“NIPSCO”), the interconnecting transmission

owner, does not oppose it.


2
  MISO Tariff, Attachment X, Generator Interconnection Procedures, § 3.3.1 (“For Existing Generating Facilities
that have not yet reached Commercial Operation, the specified Commercial Operation Date in the GIA of a
Replacement Generating Facility shall be no later than the specified Commercial Operation Date in the GIA of the
Existing Generating Facility.”).
3
 See Vistra Corp. et al., 191 FERC ¶ 61,236 at P 4 (2025) (granting waiver of the commercial operation date to
extend the commercial operation date in the forthcoming replacement GIA).

                                                        2

DCACTIVE-88090505.7
         Foundry Works also respectfully requests that the Commission issue an order granting the

requested relief no later than October 19, 2026. Timely action is critical to afford Foundry Works

and AES Indiana the ability to satisfy a November 1, 2026 contractual milestone under their

agreement, preserve the Project’s continued commercial viability, and ensure its ability to support

the resource adequacy needs of AES Indiana’s service territory.

I.      COMMUNICATIONS

        Please address all notices and communications regarding this proceeding to the following

persons who are also designated for service in this proceeding:

         Will Borders, Chief Compliance Officer                   Tyler O’Connor
         Nicole Luckey, Senior Vice President, Regulatory         Kathryn Douglass
         Affairs                                                  Crowell & Moring LLP
         Invenergy LLC                                            600 Fifth St NW
         One South Wacker Drive, Suite 1800 Chicago, IL           Washington, D.C. 20001
         60606                                                    Tel: 202-624-2500
         Tel: 312-224-1400                                        toconnor@crowell.com
         NLuckey@invenergy.com                                    kdouglass@crowell.com
         Ferccompliance@invenergy.com

II.     BACKGROUND

        A.      Applicable GIA and MISO Tariff Provisions

        Article 2.3.1 of Foundry Works’ GIA provides, in relevant part, that:

                This GIA shall be terminated by Transmission Provider if the
                Generating Facility or a portion of the Generating Facility fails to
                achieve Commercial Operation by the Commercial Operation Date
                established in accordance with Section 4.4.4 of Attachment X,
                including any extension provided thereunder, or has ceased
                Commercial Operation for three (3) consecutive years, beginning
                with the last date of Commercial Operation for the Generating
                Facility, after giving Interconnection Customer ninety (90) Calendar
                Days advance written notice.

        And Section 4.4.4 of Attachment X to the MISO Tariff states, in relevant part, that:

                At the completion of the Definitive Planning Phase, the Commercial
                Operation Date shall be set forth in a GIA. Consistent with Article
                2.3.1 of the GIA, once that GIA is executed or filed unexecuted, if
                the Generating Facility fails to reach Commercial Operation by the
                                                 3

DCACTIVE-88090505.7
                    Commercial Operation Date set forth in the GIA, such Commercial
                   Operation Date as set forth in the GIA may be extended by
                   Interconnection Customer for a period up to three (3) consecutive
                   years, after which Transmission Provider shall terminate the GIA if
                   the Generating Facility has still failed to reach Commercial
                   Operation.

           The GIA provides for a commercial operation date of December 15, 2024,4 which may be

extended for a maximum of three years under the MISO Tariff, until December 15, 2027.5 Absent

a waiver, MISO is obligated to terminate the GIA, and by extension, any replacement GIA, if

commercial operation is not achieved by that date.

           B.      The Foundry Works Project

           Foundry Works has been developing a 200 MW solar generation facility in Lake County,

Indiana that will interconnect to the transmission system owned by NIPSCO and operated by

MISO. Foundry Works executed the original GIA on March 2, 2022, which was later amended on

June 28, 2023.

           Foundry Works has been steadfastly working to advance the Project as a solar generating

facility and fully expected to achieve commercial operation by December 15, 2027. It has made

significant progress in reaching its milestones required under the GIA. As of the date of this filing,

Foundry Works has expended approximately $38 million to develop the Project, secured 100% of

the land rights, and funded all network upgrades, which are under construction and nearly

complete. Foundry Works has also obtained the necessary permits for the solar Project, conducted

engineering and design work, and purchased equipment with long-lead times, including the main

power transformers. However, as discussed below, circumstances outside Foundry Works’ control




4
    See Foundry Works GIA, Appendix B (Milestones).
5
    MISO Tariff, Attachment X, § 4.4.4.

                                                      4

DCACTIVE-88090505.7
 have delayed the Project such that it will not meet its commercial operation date of December 15,

2027.

                 1.       The Midwest’s Emergent Need for High Capacity Resources has
                          Delayed the Project’s Development.

        Unanticipated and significant resource adequacy challenges are currently impacting the

country, and in particular, the Midwest. Data centers, artificial intelligence, and the addition of

other large loads are increasing the demand for electricity, which has exacerbated resource

adequacy and reliability risks. According to the North American Electric Reliability Corporation’s

Long-Term Reliability Assessment issued on January 23, 2026, the Midwest region—where the

Project is located—is classified as “high risk” beginning in 2028, meaning “today’s demand

forecasts and resource projections indicate a shortfall in future planned resources for expected (i.e.,

most likely, aka 50/50) demand and typical resource performance.”6

        Utilities are increasingly employing BESS to protect consumers from resource adequacy

shortfalls and to mitigate rising electricity prices.7 BESS projects provide significant capacity

value, dispatch energy during periods of high-demand or low-generation, and alleviate congestion.

BESS projects also support grid reliability by providing ancillary services.

        AES Indiana has an accelerating and material capacity need driven by both baseline load

growth and incremental large-load demand, including new data center customers. AES Indiana

filed a petition with the Indiana Utility Regulatory Commission (“IURC”), in relevant part, for

approval to acquire Foundry Works on April 22, 2026, which is currently pending IURC approval.8


6
 North American Electric Reliability Corp, Long-Term Reliability Assessment at 12, 16 (Jan. 23, 2026), available at
https://www.nerc.com/globalassets/our-work/assessments/nerc_ltra_2025.pdf.
7
 See U.S. Energy Information Administration, Utilities Report Batteries are Most Commonly Used for Arbitrage
and Grid Stability (June 25, 2024), available at https://www.eia.gov/todayinenergy/detail.php?id=62405.
8
 See Petition of Indianapolis Power & Light Company d/b/a AES Indiana, Indiana Utility Regulatory Commission,
Cause No. 46394 (Apr. 22, 2026).

                                                         5

DCACTIVE-88090505.7
 As reflected in the recent testimony, this need begins as early as the 2028 planning year and grows

meaningfully over time. Projects like Foundry Works are critical to meeting these near-term

reliability requirements. If the Project were to lose its current queue position or be delayed, AES

Indiana would face a compressed timeline to procure replacement capacity, likely at higher cost

and with increased execution risk. This could result in upward pressure on customer rates and

reduced flexibility in maintaining a reliable and cost-effective resource portfolio. Accordingly,

preserving the Project’s timeline and interconnection status is important to ensuring continued

reliability and affordability for AES Indiana’s customers. To that end, on October 15, 2025,

Foundry Works submitted a generator replacement request pursuant to the MISO generator

interconnection procedures in Attachment X, Section 3.7.1 to effectuate the fuel change from a

solar facility to a BESS. MISO released the final version of the system impact study and the short

circuit study on August 4, 2026, which confirmed that there would be no system impacts or

restrictions on the requested switch from solar to BESS.

        With MISO’s approval of the Project’s fuel change secured, Foundry Works is prepared to

expeditiously bring the Project to commercial operation. However, that process will take time.

Foundry Works has already begun the local permitting process for the BESS and met with Lake

County officials several times about the re-zoning and special exception permit process. The

property that is planned to host the storage project was successfully re-zoned on June 9, 2026,

from Agricultural zoning to Conditional Development, which is a prerequisite to obtaining a BESS

Special Exception permit in Lake County, Indiana. Foundry Works is currently preparing the

application for a BESS Special Exception permit, and it anticipates that the special exception

permitting process will be completed by the fourth quarter of 2026. After the BESS special

exception is obtained (the final discretionary local permit), Foundry Works will obtain the



                                                6

DCACTIVE-88090505.7
 remaining administrative construction permits (Drainage Board approval, Final Development Plan

approval, and Building Permit approval) by Q1 2027, after which it plans to commence the

Project’s construction in Spring 2027, immediately after the winter shutdown period typical for

projects in the Midwest. Foundry Works contractors have advised that construction will take

approximately 12-16 months and then testing and commissioning will take up to approximately 3-

6 months.

        Based on this development timeline and construction timeline, Foundry Works will not

meet the commercial operation date of December 15, 2027, but expects the Project will achieve

commercial operation by December 15, 2028.

                2.    Foundry Works is Committed to Developing the Project.

        Foundry Works is working diligently to develop the Project and expeditiously meet the

region’s resource adequacy needs. Foundry Works has spent $38 million developing the Project

and already taken significant steps to develop the BESS facility, including securing and

maintaining site control and land rights, conducting design and engineering studies for the BESS

facility, rezoning the property, and coordinating with county officials and local stakeholders to

advance permitting for the BESS. Foundry Works has also completed all studies for the BESS and

received MISO’s approval to switch fuel sources. Foundry Works will also use the equipment it

has already purchased for the previously planned solar Project, including the main power

transformer, for the BESS, thereby avoiding supply chain delays that are delaying other high-

capacity projects.

        Foundry Works has site control and land rights and has fully funded the network upgrades,

which are under construction and very near to completion. As noted above, Foundry Works also

executed an agreement that will allow AES Indiana to support its urgent resource adequacy needs.



                                                7

DCACTIVE-88090505.7
 Foundry Works has therefore demonstrated its commitment to bringing the Project to completion

and granting this waiver request will ensure these development efforts do not go to waste.

III.    REQUEST FOR WAIVER

         Foundry Works requests waiver to permit a commercial operation date of December 15,

2028, so that the Project can be constructed and used to serve data center load. The Commission

has granted tariff waivers in similar circumstances where (1) the applicant acted in good faith; (2)

the requested relief is of limited scope; (3) the requested relief addresses a concrete problem; and

(4) the requested relief does not have undesirable consequences, such as harming third parties.9 As

illustrated below, Foundry Works meets these criteria.

        A.      Foundry Works Acted in Good Faith

        Foundry Works has acted in good faith to diligently advance the Project. Foundry Works

has been actively developing the Project and expected it would achieve commercial operation by

December 15, 2027. Recent resource adequacy challenges have created circumstances beyond

Foundry Works’ control that have warranted the change to a BESS to better serve the needs of

utilities serving data center load. Foundry Works has acted in good faith to meet the region’s and

AES Indiana’s capacity needs by pursuing the fuel replacement and significantly progressing the

Project as explained above in Section II(B). Foundry Works worked with MISO and NIPSCO to

coordinate the generator replacement process and ensure that all of its financial obligations under

the GIA are met under the originally contemplated schedule. Foundry Works fully funded the

Project’s network upgrades and made other significant investments totaling approximately $38




9
 See e.g., Vacherie Solar Energy Center, LLC, 193 FERC ¶ 61,165 (2025) (“Vacherie”) (granting a waiver to
provide a two-year extension of the commercial operation deadline); Hecate Grid Swiftsure, LLC, 187 FERC ¶
61,141 (2024); Front Range-Midway Solar Project, LLC, 183 FERC ¶ 61,060 (2023); Liberty County Solar Project,
LLC, 179 FERC ¶ 61,213 (2022); Front Range-Midway Solar Project, LLC, 179 FERC ¶ 61,092 (2022).

                                                      8

DCACTIVE-88090505.7
 million, illustrating Foundry Works’ commitment to achieving commercial operation and

supporting the local and MISO-wide region.

           The Commission has granted waivers where the applicant has acted in good faith by

spending significant resources, time, and effort in developing its project.10 This includes where the

developer needed an extension to complete construction of a project changing its fuel type.11 In

such instances, the Commission found good faith where the developer had conducted engineering

and design tasks, secured necessary land rights for the project, procured necessary equipment,12

obtained site control, satisfied payment obligations under its GIA, and whose commercial

arrangement was depending upon the Commission granting the waiver request.13 Here too,

Foundry Works has acted in good faith.

           B.       The Requested Waiver is Limited in Scope

           The requested waiver is limited in scope because it would only permit a twelve-month

extension of the commercial operation date. The waiver would not relieve Foundry Works of any

financial requirements, nor would it provide for an open-ended schedule extension. The request is

a one-time waiver specific to the commercial operation date and will only waive the Tariff

provisions to allow an extension of the commercial operation date so that MISO is not required to

terminate the GIA if Foundry Works cannot meet the commercial operation date.14 The waiver

                                                           9

DCACTIVE-88090505.7
 request is tailored to the amount of time it will take Foundry Works to finish development and

construction of the Project.

           C.       The Requested Waiver Addresses a Concrete Problem

           The requested waiver would address a concrete problem by ensuring that the Project will

have sufficient time to complete construction without having its GIA terminated.15 Foundry Works

is actively developing its Project to provide much needed capacity for AES Indiana and within

MISO. Foundry Works has obtained completed generator replacement studies from MISO, and is

proceeding with Project development. Despite these efforts, Foundry Works will not be able to

achieve commercial operation by the required deadline due to circumstances outside of its control,

as discussed in Section II(B) above. Foundry Works needs approximately 18 to 24 months to

complete the development and construction process after it receives BESS permits in Q1 2027. As

such, it will not meet the current commercial operation date, but it expects the Project to achieve

commercial operation by December 15, 2028. Granting the requested waiver would provide

Foundry Works the necessary time to finish permitting and constructing the BESS without having

its interconnection rights terminated.16

           D.       The Requested Waiver Would Not Cause Undesirable Consequences

           The requested waiver will not have undesirable consequences or harm third parties.

Foundry Works has funded its network upgrades, which are under construction and thus no other

interconnection customer will be harmed by granting the request.17


15

et al., 191 FERC ¶ 61,236 at P 18; Shenandoah Hills Wind Project, LLC, 186 FERC ¶ 61,070 at P 28 (finding that
granting waiver would allow the developer time to complete regulatory processes and construction of the project).
17
   Id. at P 29 (finding that granting a waiver to extend the commercial operation date would not harm other
customers where the developer fully funded assigned network upgrades); Vacherie, 193 FERC ¶ 61,165 at P 24
(finding a waiver to extend the commercial operation deadline would not cause undesirable consequences where
network upgrades were fully funded).

                                                          10

DCACTIVE-88090505.7
         Instead, granting a waiver will benefit third parties by enabling AES Indiana to reliably

serve its growing load, thereby alleviating the strain of increased demand on the system and

reducing the risk of supply shortfalls and instability. By providing a waiver for the Project, the

Commission can bolster resource adequacy in MISO at a time when it is sorely needed.

IV.     REQUEST FOR EXPEDITED ACTION

        Foundry Works respectfully requests that the Commission issue an order granting the

requested relief by October 19, 2026. As noted above, Foundry Works has executed an agreement

that will allow AES Indiana to purchase the company and use the Project to serve its customers.

AES Indiana sought Indiana state regulatory approval on April 22, 2026, and a decision is expected

in the fall of 2026. It is critical that the Commission grant waiver by October 19, 2026 to enable

the Project to achieve a November 1, 2026 contractual milestone required under its agreement with

AES Indiana, meet its commercial operation date, and ensure AES Indiana can employ the Project

to serve its contracted data center load.

V.      CONCLUSION

        For the foregoing reasons, Foundry Works respectfully requests that the Commission issue

an order granting the requested waiver of Article 2.3.1 of the GIA and Section 4.4.4 of Attachment

X to the MISO Tariff by October 19, 2026, to permit a commercial operation date of December

15, 2028.
